title: Hardware behavior becomes physical geometry
caption: Architecture and RTL describe intended behavior. Implementation must satisfy timing, power and manufacturing rules before the layout is released.

nodes.label: Architecture
nodes.detail: Choose computing blocks for the intended workloads.

nodes.label: RTL
nodes.detail: Describe concurrent state and operations.

nodes.label: Implementation
nodes.detail: Map, place and connect the circuit.

nodes.label: Manufacturable layout
nodes.detail: Check geometry against the process requirements.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: Different verification methods provide complementary evidence
caption: A perfectly fabricated design can still be logically wrong. These methods examine the design before manufacturing but retain model and coverage limits.

nodes.label: Simulation
nodes.detail: Exercise a software model with selected tests.

nodes.label: Formal checks
nodes.detail: Prove specified properties within a defined model.

nodes.label: Emulation
nodes.detail: Run longer behavior on a hardware-based representation.

nodes.label: Verification evidence
nodes.detail: Judge coverage against the intended function and risks.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: A GPU product joins several manufacturing streams
caption: The design company coordinates process, package, test and system requirements across the organizations that supply the physical product.

nodes.label: Design team
nodes.detail: Defines architecture and implementation requirements.

nodes.label: Foundry
nodes.detail: Fabricates the logic dies in a qualified process.

nodes.label: Memory maker
nodes.detail: Supplies DRAM dies and tested HBM stacks.

nodes.label: Package integration
nodes.detail: Combines the required pieces and interfaces.

edges.label: package, test, power and thermal requirements

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: A package is only one level of the system
caption: Board support, power conversion, networking and cooling appear as the product grows into a complete rack. Quantities at one level do not automatically describe another.

nodes.label: GPU package
nodes.detail: Compute and nearby memory form a component.

nodes.label: Module
nodes.detail: Adds board support and local power conversion.

nodes.label: Server
nodes.detail: Combines modules with host and network resources.

nodes.label: Rack
nodes.detail: Adds shared infrastructure and system-scale connections.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: Communication connects multiple compute islands
caption: A fabric’s topology and software behavior affect how well processors cooperate. Local memory, GPU links and the external network are separate constraints.

nodes.label: GPU and HBM
nodes.detail: Compute has nearby working data.

nodes.label: Peer GPU
nodes.detail: A neighboring processor holds other data and work.

nodes.label: Local switching
nodes.detail: Routes traffic inside the linked group.

nodes.label: Network
nodes.detail: Connects servers or larger groups.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: Cost share and bottleneck are different questions
caption: A cheap unavailable input can limit an expensive system. Capacity, utilization and allocation must be stated for the relevant process or product.

nodes.label: Capacity
nodes.detail: How much qualified output is available under stated conditions?

nodes.label: Utilization
nodes.detail: How much of that capability is being used?

nodes.label: Allocation
nodes.detail: Which products or customers can access it?

nodes.label: Cost accounting
nodes.detail: Which expenses are counted at this stage and unit?
